26.0.0.en: Curtain: a rectangular piece of cloth.

26.0.1.en: Fine twined linen: linen made of threads twisted together to form a multi-stranded thread, from which this piece of cloth is woven.

26.0.4.en: 1- The first covering that a person sees on entering the Holy Place or the Holy of Holies is made of linen, embroidered with cloth of blue, purple and scarlet. The linen signifies purity, the blue signifies heaven, the purple signifies kingship, and the scarlet signifies redemption and blood (figs. 5, 6).

26.0.5.en: 2- The number 10 signifies the commandments, for the word of God is the basis of the relationship between man and God, so that He may meet with him.

26.0.6.en: 3- A picture of angels of the order of the Cherubim is embroidered on the curtain in order to proclaim:

26.0.7.en: a- The presence of God and heaven.

26.0.8.en: b- The justice of God, which is satisfied when it sees the blood of the sacrifices, which signifies the blood of Christ.

26.0.9.en: c- To encourage us to join the angels in praising God.

26.0.10.en: The joined set. The joined set. 50 loops on each side. 10 cubits (the roof). 9 cubits. 9 cubits (the north side) (the south side). A cubit. The colored curtains. 5 curtains, their length 20 cubits. Two loops through which a gold clasp passes. Folded curtains. The entrance. Goats' hair curtains cover the colored curtains. The colored curtains cover the whole tabernacle from below and hang down from them at the back, and do not hang down from them. They touch the boards, and the curtains. A part. Something. And a cubit rises from the ground, of goats' hair, on the outside. And the clasps above one another.

26.0.11.en: Figure (5:) The curtains of the linen covering and the goats' hair covering

26.1.0.en: The curtain: a rectangular piece of cloth made of linen, 28 cubits long, which is the product of (7 x 4), that is, the work of the Holy Spirit, signified by the number (7), in the whole world, signified by the number (4). The width of the curtain is (4) cubits, which signifies the world with its four corners, so the curtain proclaims the work of God in the world. All the curtains are equal in length and width.

26.2.1.en: Every five curtains are sewn together, so that in the end we have two large pieces of cloth, each measuring 28 x 20 cubits.

26.3.0.en: Loops: the plural of a loop, which is a small opening in the cloth made with blue thread, that is, of a blue color.

26.3.1.en: Edge: the end of the curtain, 28 cubits long.

26.3.2.en: The coupling: the piece of cloth in which five curtains are joined.

26.3.3.en: Loops are made on the edge of the coupling along the 28 cubits.

26.4.0.en: Fifty loops are made on the edge of each coupling, opposite one another, and the distance between one loop and the next is about 28 cm. The number 50 signifies the Holy Spirit who descended on the day of Pentecost. The two large curtains signify the Gentiles and the Jews, and what binds them together is the Holy Spirit, who leads them to faith in Christ.

26.5.0.en: Clasps: the plural of a clasp, which is a metal alloy that can be bent like wire.

26.5.1.en: Fifty gold clasps are made, each one to join two loops together, and they are made of gold, which signifies heaven and divinity, so that whoever enters the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies may sense the presence of God.

26.5.2.en: Thus the two large pieces of cloth, each measuring 28 cubits x 20 cubits, are joined together by means of the loops and clasps and become a single piece of cloth measuring 28 cubits x 40 cubits. In practical terms, the covering was made of two pieces joined by clasps so that each piece could be carried separately when moving camp.

26.5.3.en: The number 40 signifies the Ten Commandments carried out in the whole world with its four corners (10 x 4). The large piece of cloth measuring 28 x 40 is placed so that the side 28 long runs from north to south, that is, it covers the roof, which is 10 cubits, and hangs down 9 cubits on each of the two sides, while the side 40 cubits long runs from east to west, 30 cubits of it covering the roof and 10 cubits hanging down at the back of the tabernacle, that is, representing the west wall of the Holy of Holies, so that the west side is covered down to the ground, while the north and south sides are a cubit above the ground on each side.

26.5.4.en: The tent of meeting proclaims from within that it is heaven, and it shows the justice of God in the Cherubim, so as to impart the fear of God to those who enter. You too, in the Church, may you sense the presence of God and the fear of Him, in addition to His love, which sends angels to you to help you in your striving.

26.6.0.en: The second covering is made of goats' hair and is made like the first covering, from a set of curtains, but their number here is (11) curtains instead of (10) curtains (figs. 5, 6). Figure (6:) The coverings of the tent

26.7.0.en: It is noted here that the size of the curtains made of goats' hair is longer than the linen curtains mentioned before, for the size of each curtain is (30 x 4) cubits. This is so that it covers the tent on its north and south sides and reaches the ground, and whoever enters the tent sees the linen covering and one cubit at the bottom, next to the ground, of the goats' hair covering.

26.8.0.en: Five curtains of goats' hair are sewn together, so that their size is (20 x 30) cubits, which equals (5 x 4 x 30) cubits, while the other six curtains are sewn together to become one piece called the coupling, whose size is (6 x 4 x 30) cubits, that is, (24 x 30) cubits.

26.8.1.en: These two couplings are joined together with loops and clasps as in the linen covering mentioned before, and they form the second covering of the tent, which is placed over the linen covering, so that its total length is 44 x 30 cubits. The thirty cubits cover the roof and the two sides, on the north and south, while the length of 44 covers the roof and the back of the tent, that is, the west side. As for the door of the Holy Place, one curtain 4 cubits long hangs down over it from above, and six cubits from the ground up to the curtain remain without a covering of goats' hair.

26.9.0.en: Fifty loops are made on the edge of each coupling, opposite the other, in the second covering made of goats' hair.

26.10.0.en: The clasps here are made of bronze, which signifies earnestness and spiritual striving, or steadfastness in striving. They join the fifty loops, and the distance between one loop and the next is about 30 cm, and thus the two pieces of cloth are joined to form a covering 44 x 30 cubits long. It is noted that the joining of the two couplings will be above and around the veil that separates the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies.

26.11.0.en: The overhanging part is half of the curtain, that is, half of the coupling, one part of which is on the roof, while the other part hangs down on the west side.

26.11.1.en: The coupling, which is also called the curtain and includes 5 curtains, will cover the Holy of Holies, which is ten cubits, and then it hangs down at the back of the house, that is, the west side, to a height of ten cubits.

26.12.0.en: It is noted that the second covering, of goats' hair, has a width of (30) cubits, that is, two cubits longer than the linen covering, so it covers one cubit more than the linen covering on each side and reaches the ground on the north and south sides.

26.13.0.en: The third covering of the tent, which is placed over the two previous coverings, is made of rams' skins, tanned or dyed red, as a reference to the blood of Christ. It is a stronger and poorer covering, that is, not precious like the previous coverings. It protects the previous coverings and the tent from rain and dust. Then a fourth, thick covering, stronger than the third, is placed on it, made of badgers' skins, which is poorer than the three previous coverings and stronger, to protect them from rain and wind. No measurements are mentioned for the third and fourth coverings, but it is implicitly understood that they are longer than the previous coverings in order to cover them completely, especially the fourth covering, because the thick covering may be somewhat domed over the roof, which helps the rainwater run down on both sides of the tabernacle (figs. 1, 6). It is noted that the tent is very precious in its coverings on the inside but poorer in its outer coverings, which people see, like Christ, who is God, and in whom are all the treasures of knowledge, wisdom and love, but from the outside is a suffering and crucified man. After His likeness is the Christian, in whom the Holy Spirit comforts him and gladdens him, but on the outside he is suffering and persecuted by the world.

26.13.1.en: Seek the virtues of others that are hidden within them, and do not judge by appearance, so that you may discover God dwelling in them.

26.14.0.en: The tabernacle: it is so called because God dwells in it in the midst of His people; it is also called the tent of meeting because He meets with His people in it; it is also called the tent of the testimony because in it are the two tablets of the testimony, that is, the Ten Commandments, which are the words of God that bear witness to Him; and it is also called the house of the Lord because He dwells in it.

26.14.1.en: Wooden boards are made for the tabernacle, that is, for the Holy of Holies and the Holy Place, representing the north, west and south walls of the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies. They are made of acacia wood, which is durable wood that woodworms do not attack, that is, it lasts a long time without decay, as a reference to the pure and holy humanity of Christ (figs. 7, 8). 10 cubits. 6 boards. The double board. Two tenons joined to one another. Figure (7) The boards of the tabernacle. The double board. The double board. 6 boards. The north wall (20 boards). The south wall (20 boards). 20 boards. The width of the board is 1.5 cubits. Each board has 3 rings through which the bars pass. Two tenons joined. The hangings. 5 pillars to carry one another. The curtain of the entrance. Figure (8) The boards of the tabernacle

26.15.0.en: Each board is 10 cubits long, that is, the height of the Holy Place or the Holy of Holies from the ground to the roof is 10 cubits, while the width of the board is a cubit and a half, but its thickness is not mentioned.

26.16.0.en: Two tenons are made for each board, fixed in it or in one piece with it. This board could be several boards fastened completely together to form one board.

26.17.0.en: The number of boards toward the south, that is, the right, is twenty boards, and each board is a cubit and a half wide, so the total width of the boards, if they are set close together, is 30 cubits, which is the length of the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies. It is understood from this that the south wall is a complete wooden wall 10 cubits high and 30 cubits long.

26.18.0.en: Each tenon of the board is placed in a silver base, which represents the foundation for the two tenons of the board, or for the whole tabernacle. And since we have 20 boards, we need 40 bases, which are dug into the ground and into which the tenons of the boards are fitted, so that the wooden wall is fixed in the ground by means of the silver bases. Silver signifies the word of God, for the foundation of the relationship with God is attachment to His word, and Christ, the Word of God, is the foundation of salvation, and the two tenons of each board signify the Jews and the Gentiles, or the Old and New Testaments.

26.19.0.en: The north wall of the tabernacle is exactly like the south wall, consisting of twenty boards ten cubits high, with 40 tenons fixed in 40 bases. The boards are set close together and form a wall 30 cubits long.

26.20.0.en: "Alike they shall be coupled at the top": that is, its thickness is double the thickness of the ordinary board from its bottom to its top.

26.20.1.en: Two boards are made for the two corners of the tabernacle, that is, at the back of the Holy of Holies, and they have a doubled thickness to secure the walls of the tabernacle, that is, the north, west and south walls.

26.20.2.en: And six boards are made for the back of the tabernacle, that is, its west wall, which is the wall of the Holy of Holies, each a cubit and a half wide, so that when they are set close together their width is 9 cubits and their height 10 cubits. In the two corners the two thick boards mentioned in (v. 23) are placed, and most likely the end of the ordinary board is fixed inside this thick board at the corner by means of a tongue and groove. In the same way the ends of the boards in the north wall and the south wall are fixed by tongue and groove into the two corner boards. The width of the two corner boards is not mentioned; it may be less, about 3/4 of a cubit, with a length of 10 cubits.

26.21.0.en: "One ring": this means the upper ring on the board, since each board has three gold rings through which the bars mentioned in (v. 26) pass. The two corner boards are each double, that is, thick, twice the thickness of the ordinary board from its bottom to its top, while the ring mentioned refers to gold rings, in which crosswise boards are fixed, as will be mentioned in (v. 26).

26.22.0.en: Thus the west wall of the tabernacle is made up of eight boards, six of which are each a cubit and a half wide and ten cubits high, while the two corner boards are of doubled thickness and their length is ten cubits, but their width may be half that of the ordinary board, that is, 3/4 of a cubit, so that part of them projects on the two sides of the tabernacle, so that the width of the west wall on the inside is ten cubits.

26.22.1.en: The boards signify the Apostles or the believers in the New Testament, who rely on the word of God in their faith, and the bases also signify the prophets of the Old Testament.

26.22.2.en: Be steadfast in the word of God and believe it however much the world opposes you, and you will be firmly established in the Church of God, enjoy His presence, and find your salvation and your peace.

26.23.0.en: To secure the boards of the tabernacle, they are fixed not only vertically in the ground but also crosswise to one another by means of crosswise boards fixed to them. These are five bars made of acacia wood, placed on three levels (fig. 9:)

26.23.1.en: 1- Two bars are placed on the upper level, on one horizontal level, each fixed in ten boards by means of gold rings fixed in each board, and the bars are overlaid with gold. They signify Christ, God incarnate, for gold refers to divinity and acacia wood to humanity.

26.23.2.en: 2- The lower level of the bars, like the upper, consists of two bars, each fixed in ten boards, and the two are also on one horizontal level.

26.23.3.en: 3- The third bar is fixed in the middle of the boards, that is, at a height of 5 cubits, and it is a long bar fixed in the twenty boards by means of rings fixed in each board and made of gold. This bar is also overlaid with gold and is parallel to the upper and lower bars and placed between them. Two bars. Rings made of gold. 30 cubits. Bars made of acacia wood. Cubits. Overlaid with gold. A long bar in the middle. (a) Bars for the north and south walls of the tabernacle. 10 cubits. Cubits. (b) Bars for the west wall of the tabernacle. Figure (9:) The bars of the tabernacle

26.24.0.en: Bars are made for the north wall of the tabernacle just as for the south, in the same form, and the west wall likewise has bars made for it on three levels and in the same form, but their length is shorter than the bars of the north or south walls, because this wall is ten cubits long, while the north and south walls are each 30 cubits long.

26.25.0.en: "From end to end" means from the first board to board number 20, that is, along the length of the south wall or along the length of the north wall, but on the upper and lower levels there are on each two bars on one horizontal level instead of one bar.

26.26.0.en: The bars are overlaid with gold and the rings are made into houses for them of gold, which signifies heaven and the presence of God, or divinity. Whoever enters the tent sees it: he sees wooden walls with golden bars fixed by golden rings.

26.27.0.en: Moses saw all these details with his own eyes for a long time during the forty days that he spent with God, and He may have given him specific drawings for all parts of the tent.

26.27.1.en: Be careful in your life to be firm in God through the means of grace, which are represented by the silver bases and the gilded wooden bars, which secure your senses and all your abilities in the spiritual life and nurture your faith, which is signified by the wooden boards.

26.28.0.en: The veil is a curtain that separates the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies and is made of linen (fine twined linen), embroidered and adorned with cloth of blue, purple and scarlet, with two angels of the order of the Cherubim drawn on it. The veil proclaims the existence of a barrier between God and man, which is sin, and which would be removed by the death of Christ when the veil of the Temple was torn. As for the curtain before the sanctuary of the New Testament, it is merely a proclamation of the sanctity of the sanctuary, but it is opened throughout the Liturgy so that the believers may see everything and even partake of the Body and Blood of Christ (figs. 6, 10, 11).

26.28.1.en: Gold rings. Two angels of the order of the Cherubim. 4 pillars of acacia wood overlaid with gold. Silver bases. Figure (10:) The veil with its pillars

26.29.0.en: God asked Moses to set up four pillars of acacia wood. Their width and thickness are not specified, but they are probably like the rest of the boards. He overlays them with gold, and they rest on a base of silver sunk into the ground, and they have hooks at their top, that is, gold rings, on which to hang the veil.

26.30.0.en: The clasps are the golden threads that join the two couplings, and the place where the two pieces meet is directly above the veil. Thus the veil screens the Holy of Holies, in which the ark of the covenant is placed, so that no one sees it except the high priest once a year, bringing with him the blood of animals, as a reference to the blood of Christ, who takes us through the veil and overcomes sin after having paid its debt by death.

26.31.0.en: The ark of the testimony is covered with the cover on which are the two Cherubim.

26.32.0.en: He places the table of showbread in the Holy Place on the right of one entering the Holy Place and the lampstand on his left, so that the lampstand is on the south side and the table on the north side, that is, the north (fig. 11). The ark. The veil. The Holy of Holies. The altar of incense. The Holy Place. The table of showbread. The lampstand. The outer court. The golden. The laver. The altar of burnt offering. Aaron. Moses. Figure (11)

26.33.0.en: In front of the Holy Place a hanging is made, that is, a curtain of linen (fine twined linen), and he embroiders it with cloth of blue, purple and scarlet by a skilled tailor (embroiderer), who is Bezaleel (ch. 31:1) and his helpers (fig. 12). Hooks of gold. A curtain of linen. 5 pillars of acacia wood overlaid with gold. Bronze bases. Figure (12:) The hanging and its pillars

26.34.0.en: The hanging is fixed on five pillars of acacia wood overlaid with gold, with bronze bases, while their hooks, that is, their rings fixed at the top of the boards, are made of gold, so that the hanging may be hung on them, so that no one sees the entrance of the Holy Place except the priests, for it proclaims the dignity of the Holy Place.

26.34.1.en: It is noted that the hanging, that is, the entrance of the Holy Place, is hung on five boards for greater security, since the priests enter by it every day, while the veil that separates the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies is hung on four boards only, because the high priest enters by it once a year on the Day of Atonement. From what has preceded we see that the entrance of the Holy Place is covered from top to bottom by four cubits (the sixth curtain) (v. 9), therefore the hanging serves as a curtain hung on the pillars to cover the entrance of the Holy Place completely.

26.34.2.en: The hanging is at the entrance of the Holy Place on the east, as is the entrance of the tent, while the Holy of Holies is on the west, for the following reasons:

26.34.3.en: 1- So that they would not share with the pagan nations that worship the sun and face toward the east.

26.34.4.en: 2- It is beneficial for the rays of the sun to enter from the east in the morning to light the entrance of the tent and the outer court.

26.34.5.en: As for the Church in the New Testament, the sanctuary in it is toward the east and the entrance of the church is from the west, for the following reasons:

26.34.6.en: 1- The first Paradise in which Adam was created was toward the east (Gen 2:8), and after our departure from this life we return to Paradise.

26.34.7.en: 2- Christ was born in the east, that is, Bethlehem.

26.34.8.en: 3- The star appeared to the Magi in the east (Mt 2:2).

26.34.9.en: 4- Christ is the Sun of Righteousness, so the sun that rises points to Him.

26.34.10.en: 5- Christ will come at His Second Coming like the lightning that comes out of the east (Mt 24:27).

26.34.11.en: May you enjoy the Body and Blood of the Lord and God's revelation of Himself in the New Testament, available to you in the Church. The bronze altar and the wall of the tabernacle
